description.narrative:
Caritas Kenema is the development and relief office for the Catholic diocese of Kenema. It is the social welfare wing or socio pastoral expression of the Catholic Church in the eastern region of Sierra Leone. It was founded as a Diocesan Development Co-ordination Committee by the then Bishop of Kenema, Bishop J. Ganda in 1973. It continued in this form until 1984 when Bishop J. O’Riordan CSSp an Irish missionary was ordained as Bishop of Kenema. In 1991/92 a relief section was established under the Diocesan structure known as the “Kenema Diocesan Disaster Relief Commission (KDDRC)”. This commission later merged with the Diocesan Development Office in 1995, and was named the Kenema Diocesan Development Office (KDDO). In 2000, the name “Caritas Kenema” replaced “Kenema Diocesan Development Office (KDDO)”
Caritas Kenema’s operational mandate is in the Eastern Province of Sierra Leone, an area that borders with the Republics of Guinea and Liberia. Caritas Kenema was the lead agency in the repatriation of Liberian Refugees and the reintegration of ex combatants during the Sierra Leone & Liberia civil wars which ended in 2002 and 2003 respectively. The two countries are now relatively calm, with no reports of significant frontier movement. However, neighbouring Guinea Conakry has just held a presidential run-off election, with the outcome awaited with bated breath. Pre-election campaigns have led to continuous clashes and ethnic tensions between supporters of the two contending candidates as well as between civilians and the security forces leading to civilian casualties. Any attempt by either of the two contending candidates no to accept the results of the run-off elections would trigger massive civilian protests in the country with its regional implications.
